Chang-Yo/Dela.description: Dela is an agent harness specially designed for SJTUer.
Chang-Yo/Dela.body:
---

**An Agent Harness designed for SJTUer**

_The world keeps changing. Dela stays with you._

---

> **Important**
>
> By downloading, installing, or using Dela, you agree that you have read and accepted the project's [Terms of Use](https://github.com/Chang-Yo/Dela/blob/HEAD/docs/terms.md) and [Privacy Policy](https://github.com/Chang-Yo/Dela/blob/HEAD/docs/privacy.md).
> If you disagree with some of the content, you may skip configuring the corresponding service and not provide that credential, so that you only use the remaining features. If you disagree with all of the terms, stop using and uninstall this software.
>
> For a demo and downloads, see the [Dela website](https://dela.changyo.me).

Dela is an agent product designed specifically for SJTUer.

Dela's core is built on Pi. All campus service features interact with the school's servers through SJTU's public APIs. Account credentials are encrypted with the system keychain and stored locally on this machine. Model service information is saved as JSON files in `~/.dela`. All data is stored locally and is not uploaded to any server.

## Feature Overview

**All sidebar feature entries can be hidden in "Settings > General > Navigation Entries."**

### Campus Information Services

- **Quick preview of Canvas course materials**: Uses an access token to sync course materials, lets you quickly view and switch between courseware, and supports one-click batch download. "Add to project" places courseware references in the root directory of the selected local project, and supports batch export of courseware.
- **Campus email**: Supports receiving and composing email for SJTU email accounts and any third-party IMAP/SMTP mailbox. Drafts can be saved locally.
- **Classroom video replay**: Lets you view your own classroom video replays in the app. Supports jumping via speech-recognition transcripts and exporting recording transcripts, and can cache full classroom videos locally. Reopening a video resumes from the last playback position.
- **Timetable**: Retrieves your personal timetable through the Teaching Information Network and displays the school's courses in read-only form.
- **Shuiyuan Community (beta)**: Securely authorizes via a Discourse User API Key to give you an alternative way to read Shuiyuan. It can also be connected so that Agents can call it.
- **Global search**: Searches content across projects, sessions, emails, course materials, and settings.
- **TODO**: The single entry point for personal schedules. Each item can have a deadline, a time slot, or be all-day. Supports completion-status reminders for Canvas course assignments. The month view supports "drag-to-create" new items, and you can switch between the month calendar and list views.

### Agent Features

The Dela Harness is built on Pi and can be used as a general-purpose agent product. Dela has received special enhancements for the Coding domain.

Nero0427/dsh-purge-lite.description: Trimmed prompt-injection plugin for DeepSeek Harness: inject your own system prompt and patch the host. Nothing else.
Nero0427/dsh-purge-lite.body:
# dsh-purge · lite

**Swap your own system prompt into DeepSeek Harness.**

A plugin that does only two things: it injects the body text into the `system prompt`, then applies a patch to the host so that it takes effect. Every other module is simply absent.

---

## Table of Contents

- [What is this](#这是什么)
- [Design trade-offs](#设计取舍)
- [Installation](#安装)
- [Upgrading](#升级)
- [Quick start](#快速开始)
- [Configuration](#配置)
- [Commands](#命令)
- [HTTP API](#http-接口)
- [How it works](#工作原理)
- [Directory structure](#目录结构)
- [Compatibility](#兼容性)
- [Version support matrix](#版本支持矩阵)
- [FAQ](#常见问题)
- [Known limitations](#已知限制)
- [Versions](#版本)
- [Upstream and license](#上游与许可)

---

## What is this

DeepSeek Harness (hereafter DSH) assembles the `system prompt` before every request: host identity segment + plugin segment + tool descriptions. This plugin rewrites that assembled result to your liking. It replaces the host body with your own text and attaches an anchor at the tail, ensuring the injection remains effective across multiple turns.

It is not a "prompt manager". There is no rehearsal console, no asset library, no skill library, no rules panel, and no online update. **The settings page has only one read-only status panel.**

| Does | Does not |
|---|---|
| Attach the body of `prompt-inject.md` to the front of the system prompt | Manage multiple prompt templates |
| Rewrite `system-prompt/assemble`, clearing the host identity segment | Provide web search, vector stores, or memory extraction |
| Apply 84 patches to the host so the approval gate and sandbox follow the configuration | Bypass server-side model-side policy |
| Provide the `/purge` command, a CLI, and an HTTP API for status queries and toggles | Automatic online updates (upgrade = re-download) |

## Design trade-offs

This kind of plugin is often written as "stuff everything in", which ends up with 300 KB of dead code inside a 1.2 MB source tree, and every upgrade breaks something. This repository takes the opposite approach:

- **Only two things are kept.** Any module unrelated to "injection + patching" is excluded from the code tree. 1.2.0 removed 13 modules (about 170 KB) compared with 1.1.90, and the patch table went from 86 entries down to 84.
- **No second copy of data.** The body text is read only from the single file `$DSH_HOME/prompt-inject.md`. No database, no sync copies.
- **Patches are reversible.** Every host change is backed up from the original first, and `--revert` restores them one by one. If a restore fails, uninstall aborts rather than leaving a half-finished state.
- **Failures are loud.** Patch drift (the host's original text changed after an upgrade, so the pattern no longer matches) is explicitly marked `drifted` instead of being silently skipped.

OleksiyPenkov/MyHomeLib.body:
# MyHomeLib

**Ukrainian** · [English](https://github.com/OleksiyPenkov/MyHomeLib/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) · [Български](https://github.com/OleksiyPenkov/MyHomeLib/blob/HEAD/README.bg.md)

Managing a home e-book library: cataloging your own collection of files and working as a client of libraries on the Librusec engine.

## What it is

MyHomeLib is a desktop program for Windows that lets you catalog your own collection of e-book files: books are sorted by authors, series, and genres, searched by any combination of criteria, and opened in the reading program you have configured.

Besides your own collections, MyHomeLib works as a client for libraries on the Librusec engine, including Flibusta and similar sites. The catalog of such a library is connected from an INPX file, after which books can be searched and browsed locally, and only the ones you actually need are downloaded from the server.

Books are stored in FB2 format (individual files or zip archives), FBD, and any others; collection metadata is stored in an SQLite database.

## Features

**Collections**

Ozero-top/luci-app-adguardhome-lite.description: AdGuard Home management center for OpenWrt / ImmortalWrt / iStoreOS: integrated installation, DNS takeover, filtering and supervision
Ozero-top/luci-app-adguardhome-lite.body:
# AdGuard Home 管理中心

AdGuard Home LuCI management center for OpenWrt / ImmortalWrt / iStoreOS: integrated installation, DNS takeover, filtering and supervision, supporting three-step setup and low-intrusion DNS takeover.

> The plugin handles installation, DNS takeover, filtering and statistics; finer advanced options can still be adjusted in the AdGuard Home dashboard.

## Table of Contents

- **Overview**: [Structured Summary](#结构化摘要) · [Project Motivation](#项目初衷) · [Features](#功能特性)
- **Installation**: [Compatibility](#兼容性) · [Installation](#安装) · [Three-Step Quick Start](#三步上手)
- **DNS**: [Takeover Methods](#dns-接管方式)
- **Troubleshooting & Development**: [FAQ](#常见问题faq) · [Project Structure](#项目结构) · [Build](#构建) · [Documentation](#文档) · [Feedback & Contributing](#反馈与贡献) · [Security Recommendations](#安全建议) · [License](#许可证)

---

## Structured Summary

**In one sentence**: Put AdGuard Home's "installation, DNS takeover, filtering, supervision, and statistics" into a single LuCI page, done in three steps with no manual config editing needed.

> 💡 If you can install `.ipk`, use the installation package; if the package page shows `apk` or the firmware is 25.12 or above, use `install.sh` directly.

**Not applicable**: Docker, NAS, general Linux distributions; LoongArch architecture is not supported for now.

---

## Project Motivation

The first time using AdGuard Home, two hurdles are hard to get past: the core download keeps failing, and it's unclear how to connect DNS. This plugin addresses these two pitfalls:

- **No need to understand DNS**: takes over port 53 by default, automatically moves DNSMasq to 1745, and restores everything as-is when stopped or uninstalled;
- **No need to find the core**: automatically detects architecture for download, with solutions for domestic networks and fake-IP environments;
- **No need to configure in advance**: built-in accounts, rules, Chinese interface, and log retention period, so it works as soon as it's enabled;
- **Works with any firmware**: supports both old and new LuCI, covering OpenWrt, ImmortalWrt, iStoreOS and derivative firmware.

For finer control, you can still make changes in the AdGuard Home dashboard or under "Advanced Configuration".

---

## Features

### Installation & Core

- **Three-step quick start**: Install core → enable with one click → open AGH dashboard; each step shows status and failure reasons.
- **Official core**: automatically detects architecture and downloads the official version, with pre-release optional; configuration is backed up before upgrade, and failure on the pre-release channel automatically falls back to the stable release.
- **Download fallback**: progress is visible in real time, supports multiple GitHub reverse proxies, and automatically falls back to the official CDN and direct connection on failure; fake-IP environments automatically resolve the real IP.

cyanwell/dsh-agent-soul.description: A set of "soul architecture" for agents: a five-layer model, four criteria, a capability list, and one self-check. It delivers the questions and criteria, not the answers.
cyanwell/dsh-agent-soul.body:
# agent-soul

A **soul-layer runtime** decoupled from DSH. Sessions, events, memory, and persona are built in, and any harness can plug into it.

> ## ⚠️ Check the branch first
> 
> | Branch | What it is | Status |
> |---|---|---|
> | **`v4`** | **Current mainline**: standalone process, standalone UI, standalone storage | **Under active development, use this one** |
> | `main` | v3 history: plugin form, embedded in DSH | No longer maintained |
> 
> **`git clone` defaults to `main`, which is old code.** Run `git checkout v4` first.
> 
> v4 is not compatible with v3. It is not an upgrade; it is a different thing.

---

# ★★★ Read this whole section before installing (do not install until you have read it)

## 1. What it depends on

### 1. Embedded LLM (**a core dependency, not optional**)

```
Without an LLM, it can still ingest raw text, build indexes, record commitments, and decide whether to act. These are pure computation.
Without an LLM, it cannot run context-breath diagnosis (finding context-pollution points), perform semantic memory retrieval, or run any organ that requires judgment.
```

**You must configure an API key.** The default is the official DeepSeek service:

```
Config item: the llm section of config.json
  protocol   openai
  model      deepseek-chat
  baseUrl    https://api.deepseek.com
  apiKeyRef  dpapi:deepseek-official   (recommended, encrypted with local DPAPI)
             or env:DEEPSEEK_API_KEY   (environment variable)
             or apiKey written directly (plaintext, not recommended)
```

★ **How to enter the key**: after installing, open the `Settings` page. In the `Model access` group, fill in "API Key" and click save.
  It writes to disk atomically (`.tmp` → rename) and reads the value back to show you.

★ **How to verify it actually works**: call `GET /api/health` and check two fields:

```json
{ "llmReady": true,   // key can be resolved (config layer)
  "llmUsable": true,  // **the most recent real call succeeded** (capability layer)
  "llmLastError": null }
```

★★ **Checking only `llmReady` can mislead you**: it only proves the key exists, not that the account has credit.
  `llmUsable: false` with `llmLastError` containing `402 Insufficient Balance` means the balance is insufficient.

> The desktop is the best place for AI.
>
> Technology should not be lofty and remote; it should serve the people.
>
> AI in the browser makes you accommodate it. AI installed on your desktop moves straight into your files, terminal, and workflow.
> Download: https://github.com/deepseekv5/jutian-agent/releases/latest
Developed by a middle school student, seeking support,

## 📖 Table of Contents

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| [Six things, done well](#highlights) | [Four kernels — hand over your choice](#kernels) | [Sub-agents — AI dispatches AI](#swarm) |
| [Free models — AI with no barriers](#free-models) | [User extension layer — AI edits the interface](#uxl) | [Remote from phone](#remote) |

## ✦ Six things, done well

**01 — Tell it in plain language, and it acts**

58 built-in tools connect directly to the real terminal and file system. You state the goal; it breaks down the steps, calls tools, verifies, and delivers results. Not advice, execution.

**02 — Code mode**

A full development environment without leaving the window. File tree, multiple tabs, syntax highlighting, built-in terminal; a snapshot is taken before each conversation turn, so an entire turn of changes can be undone with one click.

**03 — Swarm command room**

One goal, one team. The manager splits up tasks, staff hand off to each other via @ mentions, and results are automatically consolidated and delivered. Staff can be customized, group chats can be created, and a boss can be designated.

**04 — Terminal as an entry point**

Install jtcode and summon the assistant with a single command. Works in the terminal, in scripts, and in CI, without switching windows.

hey8v0/ST-iPhonie.body:
# ST-iPhonie 📱

Put a little phone into your tavern.

Characters can use the phone to send you messages, call you, and post to Moments. Lines in the main text can be read aloud in the character's own voice. Scenes from the story can be automatically drawn as pictures. You can also read the main text as a visual novel, and when you're tired, go play a game for a while.

> **1.0.7 Official Release**, welcome to play! For recent changes, see “Recent Updates” below. The full record is in the **[Changelog](https://github.com/hey8v0/ST-iPhonie/blob/HEAD/更新日志.md)**.

🎬 **[Feature Film](https://github.com/hey8v0/ST-iPhonie/releases/tag/feature-film)** (4 min 35 sec): watch it once to see everything it can do.

## What It Can Do

### Life on the Phone

- 💬 **Chat**: QQ-style private and group chats, with red envelopes, transfers, pat-pats, voice messages, and shared songs. You can open several chat windows with one character. The wallet and shop let you buy bubbles, pendants, backgrounds, and gifts to give to characters, and characters will send you things too. After chatting, you can “bring it into the story,” and the next passage of the main text will pick it up.
- 📞 **Calls**: characters call you in their own voice, with subtitles on screen. You reply by typing. Unanswered calls become missed calls and leave voice messages.
- 🌸 **Moments** and 🗨️ **Forum**: characters post updates and like and comment on each other's. The forum has trending topics, and characters and passersby (netizens) post and reply in threads. Content you post will get replies too.
- 🔍 **Check the phone**: pick up a character's phone and look at their chats, photo album, notes, search history, and shopping cart.
- 🧠 **Memory and knowledge scope**: earlier chats are automatically summarized, and when replying, related original lines can be recalled. People on the phone only know what they were present for or were told. They are not omniscient.
- 📨 **Main text and phone**: one panel manages both directions. Messages in the main text actually reach the phone, and you can select several phone chat messages to bring into the main text, or have the main text keep them in memory continuously.

### Bringing the Main Text to Life

- 🔊 **Main-text voice**: small sound-wave icons appear beside lines. Click one to hear it read in the character's own voice. Supports Fish Audio, MiniMax, ElevenLabs, Xiaomi MiMo, and Volcano Engine Doubao voice, and can connect to voice services you run yourself (GPT-SoVITS, etc.). There is also a line mini-window, line-by-line “listen,” and “full read,” which reads a whole passage together with the narration.
- 🎨 **Main-text images**: use NovelAI, GPT image generation, or your own ComfyUI to pick scenes from the plot and generate pictures. Can reuse the character's appearance settings. Vibe can unify the art style.
- 🎬 **Visual novel**: present the main text as a galgame, with backgrounds, standing portraits, dialogue boxes, and voice arriving one line at a time. Standing portraits change expression and move with the emotion. Rain, snow, lightning, and flashbacks in the narration have staging effects.
- 🎵 **Background music and sound effects**: the story plays background music according to the scene, and sound effects in the main text play when they are reached. (Audio sources are added by you.)

# torne mobile HomeBrew Edition

An unofficial, independently developed client app for continuing to operate a nasne with official firmware from a smartphone, even after Sony's end of support. It supports iOS / Android / Mac / Windows / Linux.

## Current status

We have released v1.4.4. Distribution files (IPA / APK / Mac version / Windows version / Linux version) are available from GitHub Releases.

## Features

- nasne discovery and registration
- Retrieving information about the unit, HDD, tuners, etc.
- Recording reservations: list, create, update, delete (supports selecting the internal / external HDD as the recording destination, and creating reservations from program details in the EPG)
- Recorded title list (all titles displayed, including over 200)
- EPG (program guide) display (terrestrial digital and BS supported; drag scrolling supported in the desktop version)
- Playback of recordings (DTCP-IP; playback quality selection: original quality / mobile; seeking via seek bar and ±10-second buttons)
- Live viewing (TV viewing): select and watch a program currently being broadcast from the channel list (DTCP-IP; playback quality selection: original quality / mobile)
- Subtitle display during playback (ARIB subtitles) and switching between main and sub audio
- Deleting recorded titles
- Search, sort, and filter of recorded titles, and thumbnail display
- Resume recording playback (continue from where you stopped) and fast playback (1.25x / 1.5x / 2x)
- Keyword and genre search in the EPG, and genre-based color coding

### About playback of recordings

Playback requires DTCP-IP device credentials (a DTLA certificate and private key pair). **Credentials are not bundled with the app.** You import your own pair, obtained from your own device, via the settings screen (you can also select and load a credentials.env file in pydtcpip format). On import, the certificate format, DTLA signature, and key-pair consistency with the private key are verified, and invalid credentials are not saved. Storage is limited to the OS secure store (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore); nothing is written to plaintext files or logs. Session keys are held in memory only.

- nasne with official firmware (verified on FW 2.60)
- iOS 15.0 or later / Android 10 (API 29) or later
- Device connected to the same LAN as the nasne

mitaku/andon.description: A one-person software factory: AI coding agents take tasks from a ledger through review to merge, and call the human only for decisions only they can make.
mitaku/andon.body:
# Andon

**Andon — a one-person software factory.** AI coding agents take issues from a ledger through implementation, review and merge, and the human is called only for the decisions that only they can make.

A one-person software factory. Agents carry issues from the kanban through implementation, review, and merge, and the owner is called only when a decision that only they can make is needed. The kanban is a set of files holding each project's issues, questions, routines, and history, and it is read and written with the `kanban` command.

## English summary

**What it is.** Andon — a one-person software factory — is the package, the contracts and the documents for running a software "line" with AI agents. One long-lived container (a *cell*) is set up per trust boundary (one client, one hobby, ...). Inside it, a coordinating agent (the *Chief of Staff*) reads a file-based issue ledger, starts one worker agent per issue in its own git worktree, asks a reviewer agent of a different model family to review the pull request, and lets a gate decide from rules what can merge without a person. The human is called (the andon light turns on) only for five kinds of decisions: what to build, how users should experience it, promises to the outside, irreversible risks, and changes to the line itself. Which of these a person must answer can be delegated per project, except what to build.

- **Bypass works for all devices on the network** — phones, laptops, TVs. It is configured on the router, so clients don't need to install anything.

qing1989/SpektraLens.description: Spectral film simulator · On-device development on Android · 81-wavelength physical model, not a filter · 20 films / 8 photo papers · Full-resolution RAW export · No network required
qing1989/SpektraLens.body:
# SpektraLens

**Put a spectral film lab in your pocket.**

SpektraLens is a **spectral film simulator that runs on your phone**. It does not use a 3×3 matrix approximation or LUT lookups. Instead, it brings the spectral response of real film onto the device: 380–780 nm, one sample every 5 nm, 81 wavelengths in total. It integrates the response of the sensitive layers, dye layers, and photographic paper wavelength by wavelength, then reconstructs the result as an sRGB image.

RAW decoding, spectral development, paper printing, color grading, grain and halation compositing, and writing encoded output to disk all happen on the device. **No server, no account, no photo uploads.** The app only connects to the internet when checking for updates and downloading new versions.

---

## Why not a filter

| | Common film filters | SpektraLens |
|---|---|---|
| Principle | 3×3 matrix or LUT lookup | 81-wavelength spectral integration, physical film model |
| Data | Approximations created by makers through repeated color tuning | Upstream measured film spectral density data, unmodified |
| Results | Inaccurate when you switch to a different photo | Exposure, light source color temperature, and film stock each act independently |
| Processing location | Often requires uploading to the cloud | Computed entirely on the local GPU / CPU |

# ZVP5 · Zhenhai High School Volunteer Management Platform

> An open-source management platform for secondary school volunteer service: **activity organization → volunteer registration → hour accounting → statistical reports → audit trail**,
> with a controllable AI assistant (ZVAgent) and an administrator operations console.
>
> Frontend: Vue 3 + PWA. Backend: FastAPI + Oracle Autonomous Database. Deployed with systemd + nginx, with no container dependency.

zshebjtzs/tree-grow-game.description: Offline two player/human-machine strategy chess based on graph theory topology and Voronoi map.
zshebjtzs/tree-grow-game.body:
# Growth Tree: Graph Theory

**Growth Tree: Graph Theory** is a browser strategy game centered on graph-theoretic topology and tree-like expansion. Players establish root nodes on a randomly generated regional map, expand their influence by continually growing branches, and use the tree structure between nodes to attack, defend, and fight.

The game supports local two-player matches, human-versus-computer matches, and an interactive tutorial for new players. A full match covers match setup, map deployment, turn actions, combat feedback, and result settlement. Players can review AI action analysis and combat rule breakdowns, and after a match ends, view both sides' performance and key events, or start a rematch directly. It abstracts the connections between map regions into a graph, organizes players' forces into trees, and builds a strategy gameplay centered on spatial planning, branch management, and trade-offs between offense and defense.

**Play online:** https://zshebjtzs.github.io/tree-grow-game/

> **Detailed rules:** This document only covers the game concepts and software implementation. For the complete rules, including opening procedure, node growth limits, combat settlement, freeze mechanics, and win/loss conditions, please read **[Game Rules](https://github.com/zshebjtzs/tree-grow-game/blob/HEAD/GAME-RULES.md)**.

## Core Gameplay

Each game generates a map composed of multiple regions. Whether two regions can directly connect depends on whether they share a valid border; therefore, the map is not only a visual jigsaw of regions but also an undirected graph used to determine expansion paths.

Both sides start from their own base and build tree-shaped forces. Each node represents an outpost, and parent-child relationships represent branch connections. Players must plan expansion direction within a limited action rhythm: they need to find routes toward the opponent's base while also considering whether the structure of their own branches is vulnerable to attack.

When a new node enters a region occupied by the opponent, tree-structure-based combat settlement is triggered. A combat result may affect an entire branch, not just a single outpost. Therefore, expansion scale, branch shape, protection of key connection points, and timing of attacks are all part of strategic decision-making.

The game offers two modes:

- **Player vs. Player (PVP):** Two players take turns operating on the same device.
- **Player vs. Computer (PVE):** The player plays against an AI opponent, with a choice of Easy, Normal, Hard, or Expert difficulty.

zxsama/BilingualTranslationToolkit.description: Bilingual Translation Interface, Language Switching, Quick Restart
zxsama/BilingualTranslationToolkit.body:
# BilingualTranslationToolkit

[ZH](https://github.com/zxsama/BilingualTranslationToolkit/blob/main/README.md) | [EN](https://github.com/zxsama/BilingualTranslationToolkit/blob/main/README_EN.md)

A toolkit for displaying bilingual interfaces in Blender.

> Blender 3.6–5.3 can use the same installation ZIP. For 3.6–4.1, install it under "Add-ons"; 4.2 and later recognize it as an extension when installed via "Install from Disk".

## Bilingual Interface Translation

A bilingual interface compiled from Blender's original translation files. It supports most languages built into Blender and a degree of format definitions, and also supports blacklists and whitelists for individual words.

> First-time use:
>   1. Install the add-on
>   2. Click the `双语翻译初始化(自动重启)` button in the add-on settings
>   3. Wait for Blender to restart automatically
>   4. Click the `编译双语翻译` button in the add-on settings again

### Translating by Interface Area

In the "Translation Areas" section, turn off the "All" (`ALL`) button, select the areas you need, and recompile:

- **Top bar menu**: the top bar menu names and built-in menu items that Blender recognizes.
- **Node / Node properties**: "Node" only selects entries recognizable in the node editor's "Add" menu (excluding the "Add" heading in the menu bar and any other menus); "Node properties" includes the properties and options actually declared. Blender 3.6–5.3 series use the corresponding built-in sockets and in-node panel entries. Custom sockets, unlisted dynamic names, and content without a translation in the official glossary are not guaranteed to be covered.
- **Properties editor / Modifiers**: panel titles in the Properties editor and modifier-related entries; you can select only modifier names, categories, fields, and the modifier assets bundled with Blender.

Blender's native interface looks up the dictionary using "translation context + original English text" and does not pass in the editor or area. Entries with the same name but different contexts are still matched separately. Identical entries show bilingual text in all shared locations as long as they belong to any selected area. Other unselected entries keep their original monolingual translations.

The whitelist can add a precise translation with `NodeTree :: Add`; `* :: 文件的英文名` denotes the default context. Such manual entries remain globally effective. A legacy plain-text whitelist, when only the whitelist is selected, accepts only entries that are unique and use a non-default context; it no longer automatically expands checked areas. The plain-text blacklist still blocks all entries with the same name, and the same context syntax can be used to block specific ones. Turning off "Override original language" preserves the original monolingual language options.

### Migration and Uninstallation

If you use "Copy settings from previous version" on the Blender splash screen, recompile the bilingual glossary in the new version after migrating. You do not need to clear the configuration first. Migration preserves the original installation form: legacy add-ons will not automatically become extensions, which avoids enabling two sets at once.
